mainTopic: Leftover figs after the harvest, רבי טרפון's regret, and when one may use the honor of תורה
overview: A ברייתא teaches that once most of the fig-cutting knives are put away, the leftover figs are treated as ownerless: taking them is not גזל, and they need no מעשר. The גמרא tells three stories about this. רבי eats the figs, but רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה refuses, because he thinks the owner's invitation was only polite. רבי חמא בר רבי חנינא proves to his attendant that eating is allowed. Then an owner nearly drowns רבי טרפון, who saves himself by saying his name, and he regrets all his life that he used the crown of תורה. רבי יוחנן teaches with a קל וחומר from בלשצר that whoever uses the crown of תורה is uprooted from the world. The גמרא explains that the owner took רבי טרפון for a thief, and that רבי טרפון regretted it because he could have paid the man off. Related teachings follow: learn תורה out of love and not for honor, and do not use it as a crown or as a digging tool. Finally רבא rules that a person may make himself known where he is a stranger, and that a תלמיד חכם may ask to be heard first, just as a כהן takes first. The source for the כהן, וקדשתו, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Leftover figs become ownerless once the knives are put away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that when most fig-cutting knives have been put away, the leftover figs are permitted to anyone (no גזל) and are exempt from מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: once most of the fig-knives have been put away, the leftover figs may be taken without it being stealing, and they are exempt from tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a basic rule about figs left in the field after the harvest is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the cutting knives have been folded up, the harvest is clearly finished. The owner is assumed to have given up on what is left, so the figs act like הפקר. That is why taking them is not גזל, and why they need no מעשר, since ownerless produce is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: the knives used for cutting figs

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the background for all three stories that follow. Each story tests how far we can trust this assumption about the owner.

phrases.english: It was taught:
If most of the knives have been folded up and put away,
phrases.notes: These are the fig-cutting knives. Putting them away is a sign the harvest is over.

phrases.english: they are permitted with regard to stealing,
phrases.notes: "They" means the figs still left in the field.

phrases.english: and they are exempt from tithes.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: After most knives are put away, leftover figs are treated as ownerless: no גזל, and no מעשרות.

steps.title: רבי eats, רבי יוסי does not, and the owner invites them
steps.stepSummary: רבי and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה arrive after the harvest. רבי eats the figs, but רבי יוסי does not. The owner comes and asks why the רבנן are not eating, since the harvest is over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה came to a place after most of the knives were put away. רבי ate, but רבי יוסי did not. The owner came and said: Why aren't the רבנן eating? Most of the knives are already put away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that shows two great חכמים acting differently about the rule we just learned. It is setting up the next step, which explains why רבי יוסי still refuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי follows the ברייתא as it stands and eats. רבי יוסי holds back. Then the owner himself seems to give permission by repeating the very rule, which should remove any doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: their owner (the owner of the figs)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi and Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda
happened to come to a certain place
at a time when most of the knives had been put away.
Rabbi was eating,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא אָכֵיל.
phrases.english: but Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda was not eating.
Their owner came,
phrases.notes: "Their" refers to the figs, so this is the owner of the field.

phrases.english: and he said to them:
Why are the Rabbis not eating?
It is the time when most of the knives have been put away!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַעוּ לְהָהוּא אַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies the ברייתא in real life
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ate under the rule of the ברייתא. רבי יוסי held back, even after the owner seemed to give permission.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי still refused: the owner was only being polite
steps.stepSummary: Even after the owner's words, רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה did not eat. He thought the owner only said it out of embarrassment, not because he really meant to give up the figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה did not eat, because he thought this man only said it out of embarrassment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוסי kept refusing even though the owner invited them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An invitation said out of embarrassment is not real permission. רבי יוסי suspected the owner felt too awkward to refuse the חכמים, so his words did not show that he truly gave up the figs. This is extra caution about whether the owner really agrees.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not arguing with the ברייתא. He agrees the figs can become ownerless. He only doubted that this owner's words were sincere.

phrases.english: And even so,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָכֵיל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda did not eat,
for he thought:
it was because of embarrassment over the matter
phrases.notes: He means the owner felt too awkward to say no to the חכמים.

phrases.english: that this man said it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן לָא אָכֵיל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the puzzling behavior from the previous step
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the owner openly invited them, there should be no reason left to refuse.
steps.terutzMaskana: Words said out of embarrassment are not real permission, so רבי יוסי stayed cautious.

steps.title: רבי חמא eats, but his attendant refuses
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר רבי חנינא arrives after the harvest and eats the leftover figs. He offers some to his attendant, who will not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר רבי חנינא came to a place after most of the knives were put away. He was eating, and he gave some to his attendant, but the attendant would not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story. It is setting up רבי חמא's answer to his hesitant attendant in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attendant hesitates, perhaps worried about גזל or מעשר. His hesitation gives רבי חמא the chance to quote the source that allows eating.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Rabbi Chanina
happened to come to a certain place
at a time when most of the knives had been put away.
He was eating,
he gave some to his attendant, but the attendant would not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אִיקְּלַע לְהָהוּא אַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about the same rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם eats the leftover figs, and his attendant hesitates.

steps.title: רבי חמא quotes a teaching that permits eating
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא tells his attendant to eat. He quotes רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי, in his father's name: once most knives are put away, the figs are permitted (no גזל) and exempt from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Eat! This is what רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי told me in his father's name: once most of the knives are put away, the figs are permitted with regard to stealing and exempt from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא backs up his own eating with a chain of tradition that repeats the rule of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attendant's doubt is answered by a named source going back to רבי יוסי. The rule from Step 1 is confirmed as accepted practice, which supports רבי חמא and רבי in eating.

keyTerms.meaning: in the name of his father

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is passed down through a clear chain of names: when most knives are put away, the leftover figs are free to take and need no מעשר.

phrases.english: He said to him: Eat,
for this is what was told to me by

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael bar Rabbi Yosei, in the name of his father:
If most of the knives have been put away,
they are permitted with regard to stealing
and they are exempt from the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֱכוֹל, כָּךְ אָמַר לִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attendant's hesitation
steps.raayaObject: That it is allowed to eat the leftover figs
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition from רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי, in the name of his father רבי יוסי

steps.title: An owner nearly drowns רבי טרפון for eating figs
steps.stepSummary: An owner finds רבי טרפון eating figs after the harvest. He puts him in a sack and carries him off to throw him into the river. רבי טרפון cries out his own name, and the frightened man drops him and runs away.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man found רבי טרפון eating after the knives were put away. He put him in a sack, lifted him, and carried him to throw him into the river. רבי טרפון said: Woe to Tarfon, for this man is killing him! When the man heard this, he let him go and fled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a third, frightening story, where an owner attacks רבי טרפון for eating even though the harvest was over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון was saved only because he revealed who he was. Once the man realized he was a great חכם, he fled. The figs should have been permitted at this time, so the owner's reaction is puzzling; the גמרא will explain it in steps 10–11.

keyTerms.meaning: he let him go and fled

phrases.english: A certain man found Rabbi Tarfon
at a time when the knives had been put away
eating.
He put him into a sack,
lifted him up and carried him off
to throw him into the river.
He said to him:
Woe to Tarfon, for this man is killing him!
That man heard,
let him go, and fled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third story, where an owner attacks a חכם who ate after the harvest
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An owner nearly killed רבי טרפון for eating after the harvest, and רבי טרפון was saved only by revealing his name.

steps.title: רבי טרפון regrets using the crown of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports, in the name of רבי חנניה בן גמליאל, that all his life רבי טרפון was pained that he had used the crown of תורה to save himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי חנניה בן גמליאל: all the days of that צדיק, he was pained over this. He said: Woe is me, for I made use of the crown of תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story by telling us how רבי טרפון felt afterward: he regretted it for the rest of his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון was freed only because of his fame as a תלמיד חכם. Using one's תורה standing for personal benefit is a serious matter, and he was pained by it even though it saved his life.
steps.whatToRemember: The stories move from relaxed eating (רבי, רבי חמא), to caution (רבי יוסי), to danger and regret (רבי טרפון). Using one's תורה for personal gain, even to save oneself, troubled רבי טרפון all his life.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a lasting lesson about not using one's תורה honor for personal benefit.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel:
All the days of that righteous man,
he was pained over this matter.
He said: Woe is me,
for I made use of the crown of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how רבי טרפון felt about the story in the previous step
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי טרפון regretted all his life that he saved himself by using his תורה status.

steps.title: Whoever uses the crown of תורה is uprooted
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: anyone who uses the crown of תורה for his own benefit is uprooted from the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Whoever makes use of the crown of תורה is uprooted from the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a strong statement that explains why רבי טרפון was so pained: using תורה for personal gain is a very serious matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 told us רבי טרפון was upset all his life for using the crown of תורה. Now רבי יוחנן tells us how severe that is: such a person is 'uprooted from the world.' The proof for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The crown of תורה; the honor and status that come from being a תלמיד חכם
One who makes use of something for his own benefit
Is uprooted from the world; is removed or destroyed

phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whoever makes use of the crown of Torah
is uprooted from the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the seriousness behind רבי טרפון's lifelong regret in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using the crown of תורה for personal benefit brings the punishment of being uprooted from the world.

steps.title: Proof from Belshazzar using the Temple vessels
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר: בלשצר used holy vessels that had already lost their holiness and was killed; so one who uses the crown of תורה, which stays holy forever, will surely be punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a קל וחומר. בלשצר used vessels of the בית המקדש that had already become ordinary, since once robbers broke in and took them they lost their holiness. Still, he was uprooted from the world, as the פסוק says he was killed that very night. Someone who uses the crown of תורה, which lives and lasts forever, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי יוחנן's statement with a קל וחומר from the story of בלשצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holy vessels had become ordinary when they were robbed, yet בלשצר was still killed for using them. תורה never loses its holiness, so using it for yourself is even worse. The logic moves from the lighter case to the more serious one.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if something is true in a lighter case, it is surely true in a more serious case
The king of Babylon who used the vessels of the בית המקדש at his feast
Holy vessels of the בית המקדש
All the more so; the closing words of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: It is an a fortiori argument:
If Belshazzar, who made use
of holy vessels that had become ordinary vessels,
as it is stated: "And robbers shall come into it and profane it,"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 7:22

phrases.english: once they broke in and took them, they became ordinary
was still uprooted from the world,
as it is written: "On that very night Belshazzar was killed,"
phrases.notes: דניאל 5:30

phrases.english: then one who makes use of the crown of Torah,
which lives and lasts forever
all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That one who uses the crown of תורה is uprooted from the world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from בלשצר, who was killed for using Temple vessels that had already become ordinary.

steps.title: Why did the owner attack רבי טרפון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבי טרפון ate only after most knives were put away, when the fruit is permitted, why did the owner attack him?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי טרפון: since he ate at a time when most of the knives had already been put away, why did that man cause him trouble?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the רבי טרפון story and raises a difficulty with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1 (and again in step 5) we learned that once most knives are put away, the leftover fruit is permitted to anyone. So רבי טרפון did nothing wrong by eating. Why, then, would the owner treat him like a thief?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Tarfon,
since, when he ate,
it was after most of the knives had been put away,
phrases.notes: This is the rule from step 1: after the harvest, leftover fruit is permitted.

phrases.english: why did that man trouble him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the רבי יוחנן teaching to question the story in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story of the owner attacking רבי טרפון (step 6).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fruit was permitted after the harvest (step 1), so the owner had no reason to treat רבי טרפון as a thief.

steps.title: The owner thought he caught the thief
steps.stepSummary: The owner had been robbed all year, so when he found רבי טרפון he thought this was the thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because people had been stealing grapes from that man all year. When he found רבי טרפון, he thought: This is the one who has been stealing from us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the owner made a mistake and thought רבי טרפון was the thief who had been robbing him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner was not reacting to this one eating. He was angry about a whole year of stealing and blamed רבי טרפון for all of it.

phrases.english: Because people had been stealing from that man
grapes the whole year,
phrases.notes: The story spoke about figs, but here the word is grapes. Either way, the owner had been robbed all year.

phrases.english: and when he found Rabbi Tarfon,
he thought: This is the one who stole from us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the background of the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner attacked רבי טרפון for eating permitted fruit, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner mistakenly thought רבי טרפון was the thief who had been stealing from him all year.

steps.title: Then why was רבי טרפון pained?
steps.stepSummary: If the owner really meant to kill him by mistake, רבי טרפון was right to save his life, so why did he regret it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did רבי טרפון pain himself over it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty that comes from the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the owner was about to kill him over a false suspicion. Saving your own life is clearly allowed. So why did רבי טרפון feel bad his whole life (step 7)?

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is the case

phrases.english: If so,
why did he pain himself?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי טרפון (step 7).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new question out of the answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His life was in danger, so he was allowed to save himself; there seems to be nothing to regret.

steps.title: He could have paid instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון was very rich, so he should have saved himself by offering money, not by using his תורה status.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because רבי טרפון was a very wealthy man, and he should have calmed the owner down with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבי טרפון had another way to save himself, so using the crown of תורה was not necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saving himself was fine, but the way he did it was the problem. Since he could have paid the man off, he did not need to use his honor as a תלמיד חכם, and that is why he felt bad.

keyTerms.meaning: To calm him down, to make peace with him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון's regret was not about saving his life. It was that he used the crown of תורה when he could have used money instead.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן עָשִׁיר גָּדוֹל הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Because Rabbi Tarfon was a very wealthy man,
and he should have calmed him down with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן עָשִׁיר גָּדוֹל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and closes the רבי טרפון discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון had no choice, so there was nothing to regret.
steps.terutzMaskana: He had another option, paying money, so using the crown of תורה was unnecessary.

steps.title: Do not learn תורה to gain titles
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק 'to love ה׳ your God' that a person should not learn תורה just to be called wise, רבי, or an Elder.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: The פסוק says, 'To love ה׳ your God, to listen to His voice, and to cling to Him.' This teaches that a person should not say: I will read so people call me 'wise,' I will learn so they call me 'רבי,' I will review so I become an Elder and sit in the yeshiva.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we are talking about using תורה for personal benefit, the גמרא brings a related ברייתא about learning for the wrong reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the goal is to love ה׳, so learning just to get honor and titles is the wrong motivation. The ברייתא lists three levels of learning, and each one done for a title is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
I will review over and over

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
"To love the Lord your God,
to listen to His voice, and to cling to Him" —
phrases.notes: דברים 30:20

phrases.english: that a person should not say:
I will read so that they call me "wise one,"
I will learn so that they call me "Rabbi,"
I will review so that I become an Elder
and sit in the yeshiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by theme: like רבי טרפון's story, it warns against using תורה for personal gain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not learn תורה in order to gain titles and honor.

steps.title: Learn out of love, and honor will come
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes: learn out of love and the honor will come in the end, supported by פסוקים from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn out of love, and in the end the honor will come. As it says: 'Bind them on your fingers, write them on the tablet of your heart.' And it says: 'Its ways are ways of pleasantness.' And it says: 'It is a tree of life to those who hold onto it, and those who support it are happy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the right way to learn: out of love. It promises that honor will come by itself, and brings פסוקים to support this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honor is not forbidden; it just should not be the goal. The first פסוק describes learning that is close to the heart, and the next פסוקים show the good results that come to those who hold onto תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, the honor will come
And it says; introduces another supporting פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Learn תורה out of love for ה׳, not for honor. The honor will come by itself.

phrases.english: Rather, learn out of love,
and in the end the honor will come.
As it is stated:
"Bind them on your fingers,
write them on the tablet of your heart."
phrases.notes: משלי 7:3

phrases.english: And it says: "Its ways are ways of pleasantness,"
phrases.notes: משלי 3:17

phrases.english: And it says: "It is a tree of life to those who hold onto it,
and those who support it are happy."
phrases.notes: משלי 3:18

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַד מֵאַהֲבָה וְסוֹף הַכָּבוֹד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by giving the positive way to learn after the warning in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Learn תורה out of love; honor, pleasantness, and happiness will follow by themselves.

steps.title: Do מצוות and learn תורה for their own sake
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בר רבי צדוק teaches that מצוות and תורה must be done for their own sake. They should not be used for honor or for making a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בר רבי צדוק says: Do things for the sake of doing them, and speak words of תורה for their own sake. Don't use them as a crown to make yourself great, and don't use them as an axe to dig with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching that fits the ברייתא we just learned. It warns against using תורה for your own benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two misuses are named. A 'crown' means using תורה to get honor. An 'axe' means using תורה as a tool to earn money. Both turn תורה into something that serves you, instead of something you serve.

keyTerms.meaning: for the sake of doing them, with no hidden goal

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer bar Rabbi Tzadok says:
Do things for the sake of doing them,
phrases.notes: He means מצוות: do them because they are מצוות, not for what you can get out of them.

phrases.english: and speak of them for their own sake.
Do not make them a crown to make yourself great with them,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל תַּעֲשֵׂם קוּרְדּוֹם לִהְיוֹת עוֹדֵר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and do not make them an axe to dig with.
phrases.notes: A digging tool is how you earn a living. Don't turn תורה into your money-making tool.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further teaching to the ברייתא about learning תורה out of love, not for honor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה and מצוות must be done for their own sake. They may not be used for honor or for livelihood.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from בלשצר
steps.stepSummary: בלשצר was destroyed for using holy vessels that had already lost their holiness. So someone who uses the crown of תורה, which is still holy, deserves even worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a קל וחומר: if בלשצר, who only used holy vessels that had become ordinary vessels, was uprooted from the world, then one who uses the crown of תורה, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching is backed up with a קל וחומר showing how serious it is to use תורה for yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלשצר's vessels had already lost their holiness, and he was still punished. תורה never loses its holiness. So the one who misuses תורה is in far greater danger.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'how much more so' argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
the king of Babylon who used the vessels of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And it is a 'how much more so' argument:
If Belshazzar,
who only used holy vessels
that had become ordinary vessels,
phrases.notes: These were the vessels of the בית המקדש. Once enemies captured them, they lost their holiness.

phrases.english: was uprooted from the world,
one who uses the crown of Torah,
how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the warning in step 16 with a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: That using תורה for personal benefit is extremely serious.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fate of בלשצר, who used holy vessels that had become ordinary.
steps.whatToRemember: Using תורה as a crown for honor or as a tool for money is treated as worse than בלשצר's sin.

steps.title: You may make yourself known where people don't know you
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a person may reveal who he is in a place where people do not know him. He learns this from עובדיה's words to אליהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person is allowed to make himself known in a place where people do not know him, as it is written: 'And your servant has feared ה׳ from his youth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets a limit on the strict warning. In a place where you are a stranger, you may tell people who you are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עובדיה described his own fear of ה׳ to אליהו, who did not know him. This shows that introducing yourself is not the same as using תורה for honor.

keyTerms.meaning: in a place where they don't know him

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is permitted for a person to make himself known
in a place where they do not know him,
as it is written:
"And your servant has feared ה׳ from his youth."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:12. Here עובדיה is speaking about himself to אליהו.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְאִינִישׁ לְאוֹדוֹעֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the warning against using תורה's honor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may reveal his identity in a place where he is not known.

steps.title: What about רבי טרפון?
steps.stepSummary: If revealing yourself is allowed, why did רבי טרפון regret revealing himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the story of רבי טרפון is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's rule using the story of רבי טרפון from earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון was a stranger to the man who caught him, and he told him who he was. If that is allowed, his regret makes no sense.

phrases.english: But then the story of Rabbi Tarfon is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's rule from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that one may reveal himself where he is unknown.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי טרפון revealed himself to a stranger and regretted it, which suggests this is not allowed.

steps.title: רבי טרפון could have paid instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון was very rich, so he should have saved himself with money and not with his תורה status.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was very rich, and he should have calmed the man down with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי טרפון's case was different, because he had another way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Revealing yourself is allowed, but רבי טרפון had another choice: he could have offered money. Since he used his תורה status when money would have worked, he regretted it.

keyTerms.meaning: to calm him down with money

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same answer the גמרא gave earlier in step 13. The גמרא repeats it here to defend רבא's rule.

phrases.english: He was very rich,
and he should have calmed him down with money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון's regret shows that revealing yourself is never allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Revealing yourself is allowed. רבי טרפון regretted it only because he could have used money instead.

steps.title: Two פסוקים about self-praise seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out a contradiction. עובדיה praised himself, but משלי says to let others praise you and not your own mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא pointed out a contradiction: It is written, 'And your servant has feared ה׳ from his youth,' and it is written, 'Let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets two פסוקים side by side that seem to disagree about praising yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עובדיה praised his own fear of ה׳, but משלי tells us not to praise ourselves. Which one is the rule?

keyTerms.meaning: pointed out a contradiction between two sources

phrases.english: Rava pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: "And your servant has feared ה׳ from his youth,"
and it is written: "Let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth!"
phrases.notes: משלי 27:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks again at the פסוק רבא used in step 18 and sets it against another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק of עובדיה, which allows self-praise.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משלי says not to praise yourself, so how could עובדיה do it?

steps.title: Known place versus unknown place
steps.stepSummary: Where people know you, don't praise yourself. Where they don't know you, you may tell them who you are.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is in a place where they know him, and that one is in a place where they don't know him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own contradiction by placing each פסוק in a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where people already know you, there is no need to praise yourself, so משלי applies. Where you are a stranger, telling people who you are is just giving them information, like עובדיה did.

keyTerms.meaning: this one... that one; each source is talking about a different case
in a place where they know him

steps.whatToRemember: Self-praise is not allowed where you are known. Making yourself known is allowed where you are a stranger.

phrases.english: This one is in a place where they know him,
that one is in a place where they do not know him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction of step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים give opposite rules about self-praise.
steps.terutzMaskana: משלי is about a place where you are known. עובדיה is about a place where you are not known.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם may ask to be heard first
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a תלמיד חכם may say who he is and ask for his case to be heard first. He learns this from the comparison of David's sons to כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A צורבא מרבנן may say, 'I am a צורבא מרבנן, settle my case first,' as it is written, 'And the sons of דוד were כהנים.' Just as a כהן takes first, so too a תלמיד חכם takes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule: a תלמיד חכם may claim priority because of his status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: David's sons were not real כהנים, so the פסוק must be comparing them to כהנים. The comparison teaches that a תלמיד חכם, like a כהן, gets first place.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A Torah scholar is permitted to say:
"I am a Torah scholar,
settle my case first,"
phrases.notes: Literally 'untie my quarrel first.' He means: hear my court case before the others.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And the sons of David were כהנים"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 8:18. David was not a כהן, so his sons couldn't really be כהנים.

phrases.english: just as a כהן takes first,
so too a Torah scholar takes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְצוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further ruling of רבא about when a scholar may use his status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may ask for his court case to be heard first, just as a כהן takes first.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a כהן goes first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a כהן takes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כהן, from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask for the source of the comparison it just used. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule depends on the idea that a כהן takes first. So the גמרא wants to see where that idea comes from.

phrases.english: And a כהן, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the comparison in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a כהן is given first place.

steps.title: וקדשתו: a כהן comes first in every holy matter
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'וקדשתו.' דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that it gives a כהן priority in every matter of holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall make him holy, for he brings the bread of your God.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And you shall make him holy' means for every matter of holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and a teaching from דבי רבי ישמעאל. The list of holy matters continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וקדשתו' tells us to treat the כהן as holy. דבי רבי ישמעאל reads it broadly, so the כהן gets honor and first place in all holy matters.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall make him holy
the school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: As it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ כִּי אֶת לֶחֶם (ה׳) אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא מַקְרִיב״,
phrases.english: "And you shall make him holy, for he brings the bread of your God,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:8. Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And you shall make him holy" means for every matter of holiness:
phrases.notes: The list continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וקדשתו,' read by דבי רבי ישמעאל as applying to every matter of holiness, is the source that a כהן comes first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the foundation for giving a כהן first place, for example in being called up first.
